title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array.
think: What is the task asking? Detect if any value repeats.
What is the key operation? Fast seen/not-seen lookup.
What wording signals stand out? duplicate, seen before.
What is the brute force idea? Compare every pair.
What is the better idea? One pass with HashSet.
What are the edge cases? Empty, single element, all unique.
What is the complexity? O(n) time, O(n) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? Keep a set and return early on first repeat.
algorithm: Loop through each number in nums.
If number exists in seen, return true.
interview: I use a HashSet because this is a seen/not-seen question. While scanning once, if insert fails, I immediately know the value is duplicated.
ru: Используем HashSet: если число уже встречалось, сразу возвращаем true.
visualExplanation:
nums = [1, 4, 2, 4]
seen: {}
1 -> add
4 -> add
2 -> add
4 -> already in seen => duplicate

critical: Using List.Contains, which turns it into O(n^2).
important: Forgetting early return when duplicate is found.
nice: Not explaining why extra space is acceptable.

gaps: Important: distinguish HashSet vs Dictionary by required output.
Nice to have: explain time-space tradeoff clearly.
edgeCases: Duplicate at start should return true early
constraints: Array can contain negative and positive integers.
